messages:
alice: seeing weird memory growth on long-run inference job (50k+ tokens). heap profiles show KV slab count increasing steadily even when requests finish :thinking:
ben: can you repro locally or on staging? which model/config?
alice: repro on staging with bert-lr-v1 quant-4 -- continuous stream test harness. happens after ~30k tokens. attaching short profile and logs.
carla: curious if this is the slab merge path we touched last quarter. could be misindexed fragments that survive eviction.
dmitri: dump pls. also did kernel selection changes roll out yesterday? iirc a tiny perf patch picked a new matmul kernel that affects batch split timing.
alice: paste logs:
```
[2026-02-10T12:07:02Z] kvcache: slab_merge: merging slab id=0x7f4a size=65536 -> new_anchor=0x7f4b
[2026-02-10T12:07:02Z] kvcache: fragment idx=42 start_token=1024 end_token=6144 tag=0x9f3a
[2026-02-10T12:07:02Z] eviction: tombstone placed slot=123 tag=0x9f3a req=0x1a2b
[2026-02-10T12:07:02Z] alloc: reuse slot=123 found tag=0x7f1b expected=0x9f3a
[2026-02-10T12:07:02Z] kvcache: stale-block-detected slot=123 owner_req=0x1a2b current_req=0x4cde
```
```
heap profile snippet:
slab_count: 124 -> 186 over 2h
fragment_map_entries: 2210 -> 4120
kv_residues: 480 -> 1376
```
carla: that log line `alloc: reuse slot=123 found tag=0x7f1b expected=0x9f3a` looks like tag mismatch on reuse -> cross-request contamination. maybe eviction didn't zero the fingerprint before reuse.
ben: could also be a race between background compaction (slab_merge) and live allocation from request threads. if compaction moves fragments but doesn't update per-request tag atomically, other request can read stale fragment headers.
dmitri: we added a fast-path to avoid memcpy when kernel selection favors in-place patching. might skip a barrier in rare cases.
alice: test I ran: forcing full-barrier on reuse stops growth and prevents stale-block-detected logs. perf hit ~2% p99 increase but stable memory.
carla: remaining question: why fragments aren't freed earlier — eviction tombstone placement looks suspicious. maybe evict-mark then merge path expects tombstone->cleanup but tombstone gets reused before cleanup completes.
ben: suggestion: when placing tombstone set slot->epoch++, and on reuse check epoch equality, not only fingerprint tag. that gives stronger protection without heavy barriers.
dmitri: we need a small reproducer to validate epoch fix. alice can you run this harness with `KV_EPOCH=1` env toggle we added?
alice: running now on staging small-canary. will post results in ~5m.
kv-watchdog: deploy-bot: rolled canary build r-2026.2.10-kv-epoch-toggle to staging env cluster id=stg-3
alice: quick results: with epoch toggle enabled the slab_count stops growing, no stale-block logs for 20m run. with toggle off it reappears in ~3-4m.
carla: good signal. next step: add unit test around slab_merge where compaction interleaves with allocator thread. also add assert on tag/epoch mismatch to catch in CI.
ben: long-term: consider switching eviction to mark+defer-free semantics so compaction can't observe partially-updated headers.
dmitri: also audit kernel selection fast-paths for any memory ordering assumptions. i'll grep the commit that introduced in-place kernel and add memory_fence where needed.
alice: created issue: https://redwood/issues/INF-1729 (slab merge misindex + cross-request slab reuse). added repro harness and temp toggle. assigning to dmitri + carla.
carla: I'll add the CI test and a stress job that runs for 24h in perf infra.
ben: put the epoch toggle behind a config flag in console so we can roll in prod if needed.
alice: thanks team :thumbsup:
carla: follow-up: prioritize patch -> canary -> prod ramp. estimated 1d for fix + tests, 2d for rollout.
ben: adding blameless note to postmortem template in case we see customer impact.
dmitri: patch branch created, will include fence + epoch increment on tombstone and unit tests. ping when ready for review.
alice: saved profiler output and test logs to /var/artifacts/kv/2155555555/ — attaching in thread.
ben: nice detective work everyone. tagging @oncall in case of flares during rollout.
carla: next up: correlate kernel selection changes with batch-split histograms to rule out timing regressions that expose this race.
